claims.text: High-temperature structural and chemical stability of near-equiatomic multielement nanoparticles is primarily governed by lattice-distortion-induced sluggish diffusion.
Atomic-size mismatches and random multielement mixing induce substantial lattice distortion in HEA nanoparticles.
High configurational entropy and lattice distortion increase the activation energy for atomic diffusion.
Reduced atomic mobility kinetically impedes elemental segregation and phase separation.
The nanoparticles face thermodynamic drives toward ordering.
Suitable near-equiatomic HEA nanoparticles can be fabricated by either thermal shock or electrodeposition.
The nanoparticles begin as a uniform, disordered solid solution.
Using five or more elements maximizes lattice-distortion effects.
Comparing a five-or-more-element HEA with a binary or limited multicomponent alloy of similar noble-metal content isolates lattice distortion and mixing entropy.
The ranges 773–1173 K and 473–1923 K are service-relevant for catalytic and thermoelectric operation, respectively.
Binary or lower-order alloys have less lattice distortion and therefore permit faster atomic diffusion than HEA nanoparticles.
Faster diffusion in binary or lower-order alloys leads to greater phase separation or elemental segregation under the same thermal conditions.
HEA nanoparticles will have lower diffusion coefficients than binary or less-complex controls.
HEA nanoparticles will retain a more homogeneous elemental distribution after high-temperature exposure than the controls.
HEA nanoparticles will undergo less morphological change or agglomeration than the controls.
HEA nanoparticles will exhibit less phase separation than the controls after thermal exposure.
Greater structural stability should produce more sustained catalytic or thermoelectric performance relative to the baseline.
Support or substrate interactions can independently stabilize multielement nanoparticles.
Extreme oxidizing environments or temperatures far outside the specified ranges can cause failure modes that lattice distortion does not mitigate.
Failure to observe significantly lower diffusion, segregation, phase transformation, or coarsening in the HEA sample relative to the control would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
